title: Dowager Lady
brief_context: Namesake of the trophy won by the branch
brief_extract:
Transport costs, age and infirmity would severely limit the numbers of our members who could attend Federation meetings if they were any distance from the City, and there is evidence of an increasing reluctance amongst our members, many of whom are widows, to go out in the evening in these changing days in our society. Continuing enthusiasm
Lest you should think that we are, as a Branch, getting old and decrepit, we tell you, with pride, that we won the Dowager Lady Swaythling Trophy in the early 1970's. This sort of enthusiasm continues today, led by our good fortune in having some dedicated members who have either worked in the electrical industry or whose husbands have been involved in such work.

brief_extract:
NAEST 93/EAW JOURNALS 14

WINTER 1982
Electric Living JOURNAL
ELECTRICAL ASSOCIATION FOR WOMEN PUBLICATION
25p

Jottings from THE DIRECTOR'S NOTEBOOK

It was a great privilege to be invited to represent the EAW at the first Dame Margery Corbett-Ashby Memorial Lecture delivered in July by the Prime Minister at the Institution of Electrical Engineers, under the auspices of the National Union of Townswomen's Guilds. The venue was chosen as a result of liaison with the EAW, and it was wonderful to see the IEE lecture theatre packed to capacity.

title: Prime Minister; Mrs
brief_context: Delivered the first Dame Margery Corbett-Ashby Memorial Lecture.
brief_extract:
I must admit, however, that it seemed somewhat strange to be attending a non-electrical event in those surroundings, so familiar to us all. *
*
*
The Townswomen's National Executive held a delightful buffet reception before the Lecture, at which they, and their numerous guests, had an opportunity to meet Mrs Thatcher and, in many cases, to chat with her. Although she had come directly from the Falkland Islands service at St Paul's, the Prime Minister was evidently unfatigued and full of energy and enthusiasm for the task in hand.

title: Dame
brief_context: Mentioned as an outstanding woman of the century.
brief_extract:
*
*
*
Having delivered her address, the Prime Minister invited questions from the audience, answering many of them in considerable detail. It was particularly fascinating to learn how and why Mrs Thatcher had entered politics and it also made one very proud to hear her refer to our own Dame Caroline Haslett as one of the outstanding women of this century. *
*
*
Turning to the EAW's recent affairs, many good things have been happening.

brief_context: Author reporting on a visit to Kew Gardens
brief_extract:
Liaison Organiser Jennifer Manley reports on
A visit to Kew

Any connection between the EAW and the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew may seem on first thoughts to be somewhat tenuous but, as the group of Associate Members who I recently accompanied on a visit soon found out, electricity plays an important part in many of the Gardens' activities. Our visit coincided with a strike on the Underground, and torrential rain rather spoiled the boat trip from Westminster to Kew but failed to mar our enjoyment of the day.

brief_context: Led the tour for the group at the Herbarium
brief_extract:
They now comprise probably the world's largest collection of living plants, from all over the world. EVERY KNOWN PLANT
Under the guidance of Mrs Stubbs, Guide Lecturer, we started our tour at the Herbarium where we found our first application of electricity. The Herbarium contains dried specimens of more or less every known plant and these are used for identification by botanists throughout the world.

brief_context: Hypothetical child mentioned regarding poisonous plants
brief_extract: To protect this invaluable collection from the ravages of the Drug-store beetle newly acquired specimens are put into a freezer for a specified time — this treatment kills all stages of the beetle. Scientists at Kew receive many emergency calls from anxious parents wanting to know whether the plant that young Jimmy has just been found eating is poisonous. They also give advice on a wide variety of questions relating to all kinds of plants, including those useful to man.
